items.description: [Hoverlab] The list that follows the dropzone: complete, uploading, queued and failed rows with cancel and retry — because hiding the failure is the classic upload bug.

items.name: vijetbhat6/upload-resumable
items.description: [Hoverlab] One big file on a connection that will drop: a bar allowed to go backwards when a chunk is retried, a time estimate that is a range or nothing, and a promise about closing the tab made before it is needed.

items.name: vijetbhat6/csv-import-mapper
items.description: [Hoverlab] The screen between "file uploaded" and "data imported": source columns mapped to schema fields, with a sample value under each and required fields blocking the button.

items.name: vijetbhat6/avatar-crop-upload
items.description: [Hoverlab] Framing a profile photo with keyboard-operable zoom and position, showing what gets trimmed rather than hiding it behind the mask.

items.name: vijetbhat6/upload-requirements-form
items.description: [Hoverlab] An upload form that states the constraints before the file is chosen, rather than rejecting it after a two-minute transfer.

items.name: vijetbhat6/import-from-url-form
items.description: [Hoverlab] The import path for a file that is already on the internet, which does not need to travel through the browser at all.

items.name: vijetbhat6/chat-thread-panel
items.description: [Hoverlab] A scrolling conversation with per-turn actions, announced as a polite log restricted to additions — so a streaming reply is not re-read on every token — and auto-scroll that only pins when the user is already at the bottom.

items.name: vijetbhat6/chat-prompt-bar
items.description: [Hoverlab] The trigger menus done properly: @ and / open only at a token boundary, the query is derived from the caret so the menu closes itself, and focus never leaves the textarea — the combobox pattern, not a floating div.

items.name: vijetbhat6/chat-streaming-answer
items.description: [Hoverlab] Token-by-token text with linked citations, follow-up chips and a caret that stops the moment the stream does. The status is announced once; the prose is deliberately outside every live region.

items.name: vijetbhat6/chat-empty-state
items.description: [Hoverlab] The blank thread, answered: grouped starter prompts as real lists of buttons, each group labelled, so the highest-leverage screen in an AI product is not a centred logo.

items.name: vijetbhat6/chat-message-branches
items.description: [Hoverlab] The answers a regenerate throws away — siblings rather than replacements, an edited question that branches in place, and a plain sentence about what happens to the replies below.

items.name: vijetbhat6/chat-artifact-canvas
items.description: [Hoverlab] The two-pane assistant layout, with the mismatch nobody else states: the canvas names the version it is showing and says so when that is not the one the conversation is about. Versions link back to the turn that made them.

items.name: vijetbhat6/chat-model-picker
items.description: [Hoverlab] Model selection with the three numbers the choice actually turns on — capability, latency and cost per message — and locked models explained rather than greyed out.

items.name: vijetbhat6/chat-attachment-tray
items.description: [Hoverlab] Files staged against a prompt with a running context-token budget, unreadable files flagged before send, removal allowed mid-upload, and a send button that names its one blocker.

items.name: vijetbhat6/agent-thinking-trace
items.description: [Hoverlab] The "thought for 5s" panel: a native details/summary outside, individually expandable steps inside — buttons rather than nested disclosures, which are announced as a disclosure within a disclosure.

items.name: vijetbhat6/agent-tool-calls
items.description: [Hoverlab] Dense tool invocations that open into their arguments and result, with status carried by icon and word rather than colour, and errors marked as alerts only once the user opens them.

items.name: vijetbhat6/agent-task-list
items.description: [Hoverlab] Run status as rows — done, running, failed, queued — with native progress elements, per-task retry buttons that name their task, and progress announced from one small status region instead of every row.

items.name: vijetbhat6/agent-working-indicator
items.description: [Hoverlab] The gap before the first token: a shimmer grid, a phase label that advances as the wait lengthens, and a running counter — which is the only honest answer to "is it stuck". The timer is hidden from the live region on purpose.

items.name: vijetbhat6/agent-run-failure
items.description: [Hoverlab] The trace after something broke: retries counted in the open with what each one cost, a step that was silently worked around drawn in amber rather than green, and the raw error kept apart from the agent’s reading of it.

items.name: vijetbhat6/agent-retry-log
items.description: [Hoverlab] What the agent tried, what failed, and what it did about it — the run history a user needs before they trust a second attempt.

items.name: vijetbhat6/agent-cost-breakdown
items.description: [Hoverlab] What one run cost, per step, so an expensive answer is attributable rather than a monthly surprise.

items.name: vijetbhat6/approval-request-card
items.description: [Hoverlab] The agent stops and asks: the effect stated before the verb, choices as radios in a fieldset so picking is separate from committing, no pre-focused Approve, and the decision left on screen afterwards.

items.name: vijetbhat6/agent-diff-review
items.description: [Hoverlab] Machine-proposed row edits accepted one at a time, with before and after in real del/ins elements, a tri-state select-all that actually sets indeterminate, and a running count of what will be written.

items.name: vijetbhat6/confidence-recommendation
items.description: [Hoverlab] A suggestion scored with a native meter rather than a styled bar, banded in words as well as numbers, and showing what the model rejected — the fastest way a human catches a bad recommendation.

items.name: vijetbhat6/permission-scope-dialog
items.description: [Hoverlab] Read and write scopes separated rather than bundled, writes off by default, a required expiry, and switches that are real checkboxes with role="switch" — so the grant is toggleable by keyboard and announced as on or off.

items.name: vijetbhat6/approval-queue
items.description: [Hoverlab] Forty decisions and an honest way to clear them: bulk approve that cannot reach the high-impact rows, a select-all that says how many it takes, and the auto-approve deadline on every line.

items.name: vijetbhat6/approval-policy-list
items.description: [Hoverlab] Which agent actions run unattended and which need a signature, stated as a policy the operator can read before anything happens.

items.name: vijetbhat6/escalation-queue-list
items.description: [Hoverlab] What is waiting on a person, ordered by how long it has been waiting rather than when it arrived.

items.name: vijetbhat6/human-oversight-split
items.description: [Hoverlab] Where a person sits in an automated run, written as four guarantees rather than as a promise that a human is involved.

items.name: vijetbhat6/context-chunk-cards
items.description: [Hoverlab] The RAG debugging surface: ranked passages with similarity as a meter, matched spans in real mark elements, and filter chips wired as a radiogroup so arrows move between them.

items.name: vijetbhat6/source-citation-list
items.description: [Hoverlab] The published footnotes under an answer — ordered list, real cite and time elements, the claim each source supports, and a staleness warning written in words rather than shown as an amber dot.

items.name: vijetbhat6/knowledge-source-picker
items.description: [Hoverlab] Choosing what the assistant may read, with indexing state told honestly — a half-indexed source says so rather than showing a green tick — and the footer stating the effect of the selection, not its cardinality.

items.name: vijetbhat6/retrieval-empty-state
items.description: [Hoverlab] The refusal screen: says plainly that nothing was found, shows where it looked and the near-misses below threshold, and offers the two real ways out instead of inventing an answer.

items.name: vijetbhat6/context-window-budget
items.description: [Hoverlab] What is in the context and what fell out of it — a stacked budget with the reply reserve drawn as a segment, and the dropped chunks named with the reason, which is the part nobody ships.

items.name: vijetbhat6/retrieval-index-status
items.description: [Hoverlab] A green tick means the connector works, not that the answers are current. Freshness as an age in words per source, the headline taken from the stalest one, and a failed sync that still says what age it is answering from.

items.name: vijetbhat6/retrieval-freshness-list
items.description: [Hoverlab] Retrieved sources ranked by how stale they are, because a confident answer from a two-year-old document is the failure people do not catch.

items.name: vijetbhat6/context-scope-list
items.description: [Hoverlab] Which sources this answer may draw on, shown as a scope the user can read before asking rather than a citation list after.

items.name: vijetbhat6/grounding-split
items.description: [Hoverlab] How an answer is tied to its sources, and what the system does when it cannot find any.

items.name: vijetbhat6/selection-ai-toolbar
items.description: [Hoverlab] Highlight a passage and hand it to the model. Positioned from the range rect relative to its container, raised by selectionchange so Shift-Arrow works, and every button prevents the mousedown that would collapse the selection.

items.name: vijetbhat6/ai-inline-suggestion
items.description: [Hoverlab] Copilot-style completion in a plain textarea: a transparent-caret field over a metric-matched mirror, Tab to accept, Escape that actually sticks, and the suggestion announced rather than left as invisible grey text.

items.name: vijetbhat6/ai-inspector-panel
items.description: [Hoverlab] The model edits real properties and every change is attributed and reversible — per-property provenance in words, per-property revert, and sliders whose aria-valuetext carries the unit.

items.name: vijetbhat6/ai-insight-cards
items.description: [Hoverlab] Findings the agent surfaced on its own, paged one at a time, each stating its magnitude rather than its direction, dismissible, and carrying a sparkline that is also a sentence for anyone who cannot see it.

items.name: vijetbhat6/ai-slash-menu
items.description: [Hoverlab] The "/" menu inside a document: focus never leaves the editor, every row names what it acts on, and Escape cleans up the trigger text it inserted instead of leaving you to backspace it.

items.name: vijetbhat6/ai-action-menu
items.description: [Hoverlab] The actions offered on a selection, each saying whether it rewrites in place or opens a draft beside it.

items.name: vijetbhat6/product-grid
items.description: [Hoverlab] Responsive product cards with sale badges, ratings and a wishlist button layered above the card link so it stays clickable.

items.name: vijetbhat6/product-filter-sidebar
items.description: [Hoverlab] Category, size, colour and price facets as proper fieldsets, with colour swatches that carry their name as well as their hue.

items.name: vijetbhat6/collection-toolbar
items.description: [Hoverlab] Result count, sort and density switch — with the count in an aria-live region, since it is the only feedback a filter change gives some users.

items.name: vijetbhat6/product-rail
items.description: [Hoverlab] A "you might also like" row on native scroll-snap — touch swiping, momentum and keyboard support for free, with no carousel library.

items.name: vijetbhat6/product-compare-table
items.description: [Hoverlab] Three products side by side with the row labels pinned through a horizontal scroll, an "only show differences" toggle that says how many rows it hid, and "best" marked only where better means something.

items.name: vijetbhat6/stock-availability-list
items.description: [Hoverlab] Availability per variant stated before the cart, because discovering it at checkout is where the basket gets abandoned.

items.name: vijetbhat6/collection-story-split
items.description: [Hoverlab] The editorial header above a collection grid, carrying the four facts that decide a considered purchase.

items.name: vijetbhat6/product-gallery
items.description: [Hoverlab] Main image with a thumbnail strip built as a real tablist, so arrow keys work and the ratio is fixed to stop the buy box shifting.

items.name: vijetbhat6/product-buy-box
items.description: [Hoverlab] Price, variant radiogroup, quantity stepper and add-to-bag — with sold-out sizes disabled and visible rather than hidden.

items.name: vijetbhat6/product-info-accordion
items.description: [Hoverlab] Description, materials, delivery and returns in named <details> elements — no JavaScript, and the copy stays indexable while collapsed.

items.name: vijetbhat6/product-review-summary
items.description: [Hoverlab] Average rating with a clickable histogram — because a 4.3 of forties and fives is a different product from a 4.3 of ones and fives.

items.name: vijetbhat6/product-size-guide
items.description: [Hoverlab] The panel that decides whether the parcel comes back: what the model is wearing and what previous buyers did, above a table whose inches are converted rather than maintained twice.

items.name: vijetbhat6/product-spec-split
items.description: [Hoverlab] The specification table beside the product image, with the two or three figures that decide the purchase pulled out of it.

items.name: vijetbhat6/back-in-stock-form
items.description: [Hoverlab] The capture that replaces a dead sold-out button, with the honest caveat that a notification is not a reservation.

items.name: vijetbhat6/cart-drawer
items.description: [Hoverlab] A basket panel with the dialog mechanics usually missing: focus trap, focus return, Escape to close and a background scroll lock.

items.name: vijetbhat6/cart-line-items
items.description: [Hoverlab] Quantity steppers and remove-with-undo, with every total derived rather than stored so the basket can never disagree with itself.

items.name: vijetbhat6/checkout-form
items.description: [Hoverlab] The full autocomplete token set that lets a browser fill eight fields in one tap, plus address labels that follow the selected country.

items.name: vijetbhat6/order-summary-panel
items.description: [Hoverlab] Subtotal, discount, delivery and tax all derived from the lines, with the free-delivery nudge driven by the same threshold as the charge.

items.name: vijetbhat6/checkout-express-payment
items.description: [Hoverlab] The wallet buttons above the form, and what they do to it: the address a wallet returns is shown and stays editable, and the row disappears entirely when no wallet is actually available.

items.name: vijetbhat6/gift-options-form
items.description: [Hoverlab] The gifting step, placed in the cart where it is a choice rather than at checkout where it is friction.

items.name: vijetbhat6/gift-card-purchase
items.description: [Hoverlab] The only checkout where the buyer is not the recipient - live preview, a send date with a stated timezone, and the confirm-the-address field that prevents the expensive typo.

items.name: vijetbhat6/guest-checkout-form
items.description: [Hoverlab] Guest as the default and the whole form, with a real autocomplete token on every field and the account offer moved to the end, where it costs one checkbox.

items.name: vijetbhat6/discount-modal
items.description: [Hoverlab] The offer popup with four rules applied: triggered by intent, a decline button of equal weight, a dismissal that is remembered, and the terms on its face.

items.name: vijetbhat6/order-confirmation
items.description: [Hoverlab] The thank-you screen built to prevent two support emails: a selectable order number and a delivery date range rather than "soon".

items.name: vijetbhat6/order-history-list
items.description: [Hoverlab] Past orders with stacked item thumbnails and worded statuses — people recognise what they bought long before the order number.

items.name: vijetbhat6/review-list
items.description: [Hoverlab] Sortable reviews with verified-purchase badges, optimistic helpful votes and a real expand control instead of a fade that hides text.

items.name: vijetbhat6/order-tracking-timeline
items.description: [Hoverlab] The fortnight between buying and reviewing, answered properly: an arrival range rather than a date, exceptions above the timeline, and a copyable carrier reference.

items.name: vijetbhat6/review-submit-form
items.description: [Hoverlab] The form that produces the reviews the other blocks display — a real radio group for stars, and a prompt that changes with the rating because one star and five need different questions.

items.name: vijetbhat6/order-lookup-form
items.description: [Hoverlab] Order tracking for the guest who never made an account, which is most of them.

items.name: vijetbhat6/review-distribution-band
items.description: [Hoverlab] The rating summary with the numbers that make an average trustworthy — the count, the spread and the verified share.

items.name: vijetbhat6/warranty-coverage-panel
items.description: [Hoverlab] A verdict for this serial number today, with exclusions given equal weight to cover and an extension offered only while it can still be bought.

items.name: vijetbhat6/refund-request-form
items.description: [Hoverlab] Refunds are per line, not per order: a reason on each line that drives what is asked for next, and a running total itemising the restocking fee and the delivery rule.

items.name: vijetbhat6/refund-status-tracker
items.description: [Hoverlab] Where the money is and who is holding it - four stages, each naming the responsible party, including the bank stage every where-is-my-refund contact comes from.

items.name: vijetbhat6/refunds-overview-table
items.description: [Hoverlab] The operator queue, sorted oldest-open-first because recency is the wrong default, with blocked as a first-class status that names its blocker.

items.name: vijetbhat6/return-exchange-picker
items.description: [Hoverlab] Refund, exchange or credit decided per line, with live stock on the variants and the price difference shown before the goods are posted rather than after.

items.name: vijetbhat6/return-label-instructions
items.description: [Hoverlab] The screen between approved and posted: three drop-off methods with the thing that actually blocks each one, the packing rules that get returns refused, and a date rather than a duration.

items.name: vijetbhat6/repair-request-form
items.description: [Hoverlab] A repair is not a return - a symptom picker that filters the service routes, warranty resolved inside the form, and an estimate with its uncertainty stated.

items.name: vijetbhat6/review-history-list
items.description: [Hoverlab] The reviews you wrote and the ones you owe, with editing that is honest about being marked as edited and moderation that names the rule it applied.

items.name: vijetbhat6/gift-card-balance
items.description: [Hoverlab] A balance checker built for the two ways it goes wrong - an empty card and an expired one - answering with a transaction history rather than a bare zero.

items.name: vijetbhat6/saas-landing-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] A complete marketing page in the order that actually converts — hook, proof, substance, price, objections, exit. Twelve blocks, navbar and footer included.

items.name: vijetbhat6/pricing-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Plans, a feature matrix and a pricing-specific FAQ written to remove the last purchase objection rather than answer general questions.

items.name: vijetbhat6/waitlist-landing-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] A pre-launch page for a product you cannot buy yet: one email field, scarcity instead of adoption, and no pricing section to be held to later.

items.name: vijetbhat6/developer-tool-landing-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Install command first, real code before any prose, and a usage calculator instead of tiers — the order a developer actually scans in.

items.name: vijetbhat6/mobile-app-landing-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Store badges above the fold, the App Store rating as the first proof, and a single price — a page with one job, which is the install.

items.name: vijetbhat6/agency-landing-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] A studio site: full-bleed hero, client list, engagements described as engagements, and the actual team — with no pricing, on purpose.

items.name: vijetbhat6/local-service-landing-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] A booking widget above the fold, every price published including the awkward ones, and a footer carrying the registrations a regulated trade must show.

items.name: vijetbhat6/marketplace-landing-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Two audiences, one page: a search field and real listings for buyers up top, the seller economics below, and a searchable FAQ because they ask different things.

items.name: vijetbhat6/enterprise-landing-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Built for a champion assembling an internal case: numbers in the hero, a comparison that concedes two rows, video references, and published prices instead of a sales wall.

items.name: vijetbhat6/integration-platform-landing-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] The connector names in the hero, a catalogue with honest live/beta/planned status, four SDK languages, credit pricing, and a dated roadmap for everyone who is not on the list.

items.name: vijetbhat6/creator-course-landing-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] One person selling one course: a student testimonial as the hero because a course cannot demo, a long instructor section, one price and a refund policy on the page.

items.name: vijetbhat6/blog-index-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] The post grid, a subscribe ask that comes after the proof, and a minimal footer — no hero, because the featured post already is one.

items.name: vijetbhat6/article-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] A single post: header, byline and opening prose in one reading column, with the subscribe form after the article — at the only moment it converts.

items.name: vijetbhat6/careers-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Team first, openings second, then the questions candidates only ask after an offer — answered while they can still change who applies.

items.name: vijetbhat6/docs-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] The site navbar over the three-column docs frame. In your project this is one catch-all route — the slug picks the article, the frame never changes.

items.name: vijetbhat6/help-centre-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Search first, the six answers that absorb the most contact volume under it, and the ticket form in plain sight rather than behind a modal — a support page measured in tickets not filed.

items.name: vijetbhat6/changelog-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] The release timeline with the site chrome kept on, and the one subscribe form on the site that is not a detour — "tell me when this page changes" is exactly what it promises.

items.name: vijetbhat6/dashboard-overview
items.description: [Hoverlab] The screen an app opens on: shell, header, KPI row, chart and activity feed — numbers first, shape second, changes last.

items.name: vijetbhat6/ai-assistant-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] An agent working inside a real app: a transcript down the middle — reasoning, answer, then the one card that can act — with what it may read and what it noticed demoted to a rail.

items.name: vijetbhat6/project-board-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] A kanban board inside the app shell, with tabs that admit the board is one view among several and a header whose primary action is creating work.

items.name: vijetbhat6/customers-table-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] The canonical CRUD list — header, toolbar, sortable table and pagination framed as one panel instead of three stacked cards.

items.name: vijetbhat6/settings-account-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Profile, team, API keys and danger zone in one screen — with the destructive panel last, well away from the everyday controls.

items.name: vijetbhat6/billing-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Plan, quota meters and invoice history, with the upgrade prompt placed beside a bar that is nearly full rather than on the plan card.

items.name: vijetbhat6/login-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] A full auth page that deliberately contains almost nothing but the form — no nav, no marketing, nothing competing with the one job.

items.name: vijetbhat6/error-404-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Drops straight into app/not-found.tsx, and keeps the site header and footer — on a 404 the navigation is the most useful thing on screen.

items.name: vijetbhat6/collection-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Sticky filter sidebar, sort toolbar and product grid — with the facets dropped rather than stacked on mobile, so a shopping page does not open as a form.

items.name: vijetbhat6/product-detail-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Gallery, sticky buy box, details accordion and reviews — ordered by what a shopper needs before they can decide.

items.name: vijetbhat6/cart-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Editable lines beside a sticky summary, so the total and the checkout button survive a scroll through four quantity changes.

items.name: vijetbhat6/checkout-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Address and payment with the site navigation stripped and the order summary moved above the form on mobile — both aimed squarely at completion rate.

items.name: vijetbhat6/order-confirmation-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] The post-purchase screen, with navigation restored and a rail that shows what to buy next rather than what was just bought.

items.name: vijetbhat6/account-orders-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Order history in the settings shell rather than a second sidebar layout — an account area and a settings area are the same shape.

items.name: vijetbhat6/signup-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] The signup form with the proof under it rather than above it — the person who arrived here has already decided, and scrolling past testimonials is friction applied to the wrong reader.

items.name: vijetbhat6/forgot-password-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Password reset, plus the magic link beside it — the moment after a password has failed is when somebody is most willing to stop using one.

items.name: vijetbhat6/two-factor-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] The second factor with its fallback on the same screen, because a 2FA prompt with no recovery route is a lockout screen wearing a security screen.

items.name: vijetbhat6/sso-login-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] A domain field for the employee who signs in daily, and the capability detail below the fold for the IT reviewer who reads it once.

items.name: vijetbhat6/error-500-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Retry first, because a 500 is our failure and offering navigation implies the rest of the site works — which is exactly what is in doubt.

items.name: vijetbhat6/maintenance-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Planned downtime with an actual end time on it — "back soon" is not a time, and a maintenance page without one looks like an outage nobody has noticed.

items.name: vijetbhat6/permission-denied-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] A 403 that names who can grant what was refused, because the next question is always "then who can" and a support link is the wrong answer to it.

items.name: vijetbhat6/usage-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Consumption in the order the questions arrive: the overage warning first because it is time-critical, then the meters, then what actually happens at each limit.

items.name: vijetbhat6/invoices-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Billing history laid out for finance rather than for the user — a retrieval screen, so the table leads and the payment method comes last.

items.name: vijetbhat6/onboarding-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] A wizard for the session someone finishes and a checklist for the one they do not, with the only genuinely blocking step in front of both.

items.name: vijetbhat6/search-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Built around the state a search page is in most of the time — empty — so recent queries lead and the facets sit in a sidebar that survives growing to twelve.

items.name: vijetbhat6/agent-run-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] One run opened up in the order you would debug it — intent, actions, the retries that are invisible in both, then cost.

items.name: vijetbhat6/approvals-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] The queue, the same queue sorted by how long things have waited, and the policy that decided both — with the policy last so it is not scrolled past forever.

items.name: vijetbhat6/assistant-chat-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] The blank thread answered with real starter prompts, the model picker with the three numbers the choice turns on, and the four surfaces a session grows into — attachments, branches, canvas, threads.

items.name: vijetbhat6/agent-inspector-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] The three states an agent screen usually omits: the wait before the first token, the trace after something broke with retries costed in the open, and the diff it wants a person to accept.

items.name: vijetbhat6/retrieval-console-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Why the answer said what it said: what is connected, how stale it is, what the query was allowed to see, what fitted in the window and what fell out — plus the failed-search state a debugging tool is most needed in.

items.name: vijetbhat6/ai-editor-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Five ways to reach a model without the cursor leaving the sentence — slash menu, inline completion, selection toolbar, action menu, property inspector — and the two surfaces that say where the answer came from.

items.name: vijetbhat6/records-table-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] A table after real people have used it — columns reordered from the keyboard, a selection bar that asks page-or-all, subtotals that survive collapsing, cells edited in place, and the empty state its own filters produced.

items.name: vijetbhat6/analytics-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] The saved view and the comparison window first, because every figure below depends on both — then six charts, none of which load a charting library.

items.name: vijetbhat6/alerting-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Thresholds with how often each has actually fired, what that produced, where it went — and the digest settings that exist because of the answer.

items.name: vijetbhat6/notification-settings-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Notifications from the receiving end: the inbox you arrived from, per-event and per-channel control, and the push prompt asked after the decision rather than on arrival.

items.name: vijetbhat6/team-access-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] The admin screen a security questionnaire is really asking about — seats with the bill shown first, invitations, scopes split from bundles, sharing stated as its consequence, live sessions, and the audit trail underneath.

items.name: vijetbhat6/import-data-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] The flow between an empty product and a useful one, in the order it goes wrong: sample data offered with equal weight, a file, a URL, the column mapping everything stalls on, and an upload that survives the connection dropping.

items.name: vijetbhat6/account-setup-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] A profile form where the role options state what they actually change, the avatar crop works from the keyboard, and a navigation guard names the fields it is about to throw away.

items.name: vijetbhat6/reset-password-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] The end of the forgot-password flow, shipped with the state it reaches more than any other screen: a focused error summary linking to each field, beside a strength meter that is a real <meter>.

items.name: vijetbhat6/app-shell-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] The furniture that is on every screen and belongs to none — navbar, mobile drawer, command palette, shortcut sheet, header search, scope switcher, and the two shapes a detail view takes without losing the list.

items.name: vijetbhat6/security-landing-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] The page a security questionnaire arrives from, written to be forwarded rather than to persuade: certifications early, benchmarks with a denominator, objections in a reviewer’s own words, and a route to a human.

items.name: vijetbhat6/migration-landing-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] The landing page for a reader whose current tool already works: the migration mechanism second rather than buried, integrations stated at depth, and deliberately no pricing section.

items.name: vijetbhat6/launch-note-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] A product announcement shaped as writing rather than a landing page — serif headline, real byline, three pieces of evidence, and an endpoint card that doubles as documentation for the week before the docs exist.

items.name: vijetbhat6/single-offer-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] One thing, one price, named above the fold — for a course, a consultation or a one-time licence, where there is nothing to compare against and hiding the number answers the only question last.

items.name: vijetbhat6/plan-change-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Both directions, because only one of them is usually built: a radiogroup with the prorated charge announced as it changes, and a cancellation with the end date, what breaks, and one honest alternative offered once.

items.name: vijetbhat6/product-compare-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] The page between a listing and a product detail, with the two questions a comparison table alone cannot answer: will it fit, and can I actually have it.

items.name: vijetbhat6/express-checkout-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Checkout for the buyer who will not fill in a form: wallet buttons above the fields, and the address a wallet returns shown and changeable before the charge rather than after it.

items.name: vijetbhat6/order-tracking-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] For the customer with an order number and no account — a lookup, an arrival range rather than a promised date, and the review form where the "how did we do" email actually lands.

items.name: vijetbhat6/workspace-activity-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Backwards from now and forwards from it on one screen — a day-grouped timeline, a month grid where a busy Tuesday never changes the row height, and the state both are in on day one.

items.name: vijetbhat6/first-run-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] What the product looks like while onboarding happens: a tour step anchored to the control it explains, the skeletons of the slowest load it will ever do, and the checklist that outlives both.

items.name: vijetbhat6/about-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] No hero — a reader who clicked "About" has already read the pitch and is checking whether the company is real, so the page opens with numbers and a timeline instead of a headline.

items.name: vijetbhat6/contact-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] The form first, then the four questions that cause most of the messages — answered here, because that is faster for the sender than a reply and leaves the inbox for what needs a person.

items.name: vijetbhat6/team-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Who we are, as distinct from who we are hiring: faces, the shape of the company in four numbers, and three working commitments that could actually be falsified.

items.name: vijetbhat6/faq-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Search and browse, in that order, because the two halves serve opposite visitors — one arrives from a search engine with a phrase, the other from the navbar with none.

items.name: vijetbhat6/case-study-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] The numbers above the story, which is the opposite of how these are usually written: the colleague this link gets forwarded to needs the result in the first screen.

items.name: vijetbhat6/case-study-index-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Excerpts that lead with the outcome rather than the customer’s biography, filterable by industry — because the reader is scanning for a problem that resembles their own.

items.name: vijetbhat6/services-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] For a business that sells work rather than licences: three engagements named by situation, and prices in a comparison table rather than a pricing card with a monthly toggle that does not apply.

items.name: vijetbhat6/integrations-index-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Every connection with its real status on the card — live, beta or planned — because a directory that hides which is which is discovered at exactly the wrong moment.

items.name: vijetbhat6/integration-detail-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] One connection, answering the four questions an integration page usually leaves to a support ticket: which records move, which way, how often, and what happens on conflict.

items.name: vijetbhat6/alternatives-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] The competitor-name landing page, with a section naming where each rival is the better buy — which is what makes the other forty rows believable.

items.name: vijetbhat6/status-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Written for the person refreshing it during an outage: current state above the fold, the maintenance window as a real block with an end time, and a component list that names what still works.

items.name: vijetbhat6/roadmap-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Board plus changelog, because a roadmap alone is a promise — the last three releases underneath are what turn the shipped column into something with dates attached.

items.name: vijetbhat6/webinar-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Registration at the top and again at the bottom, with an agenda timed by the minute — so the reader knows what they are getting before handing over an address.

items.name: vijetbhat6/coming-soon-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] The shortest page in the catalog, and it still says what the product does — including what it will not do at launch. No countdown, because a clock at zero is worse than no clock.

items.name: vijetbhat6/legal-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Terms, privacy, DPA and cookies in one frame — the docs layout, because people arrive at a legal page looking for a specific clause and a wall of text makes that a Ctrl-F expedition.

items.name: vijetbhat6/community-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Member counts and reply times on every door, because "join our community" with no number reads as an invitation into an empty room — plus a digest for people who will not install another chat app.

items.name: vijetbhat6/affiliate-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Terms before the application, and a calculator so the reader sees a number rather than doing arithmetic with an ARPU they do not know.

items.name: vijetbhat6/testimonials-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] Third-party scores first, because they are the only part of the page the company does not control — and the four-star quotes stay in, because a wall of nothing but fives reads as filtered.

items.name: vijetbhat6/gallery-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] A switcher rather than an infinite grid: four named views, one visible at a time, so the page weighs one image on load instead of forty.

items.name: vijetbhat6/portfolio-index-page
items.description: [Hoverlab] A studio’s list of work, with excerpts that name the outcome and the constraint rather than the aesthetic — a contents page, not a landing page.

items.name: vijetbhat6/about-page-02
items.description: [Hoverlab] The founder’s letter instead of the evidence wall: a byline and a dateline, for a company whose best asset is still conviction rather than a six-year record — and it ends on the job board, because /team is linked from job posts more often than from sales decks.

items.name: vijetbhat6/contact-page-02
items.description: [Hoverlab] Route before you write — three doors, each with the form its sender actually needs: a calendar for a buyer, a structured ticket for a broken import. One textarea costs a round trip.

items.name: vijetbhat6/team-page-02
items.description: [Hoverlab] The team page that is really a recruiting page: it opens on the trade rather than the faces, and puts a salary band on every role — a board with three bands and one “competitive” teaches the reader which is the bad one.

items.name: vijetbhat6/faq-page-02
items.description: [Hoverlab] Objection-ordered and search-free: the questions that lose deals first, hardest at the top, because a search box over eighteen questions implies a list long enough to get lost in — and its empty state reads as “no refund policy”.

items.name: vijetbhat6/case-study-page-02
items.description: [Hoverlab] The narrative take, for a study found by search rather than forwarded by a champion: the customer’s sentence first, the numbers last, and the six weeks in the middle where the software was losing to a spreadsheet.

items.name: vijetbhat6/case-study-index-page-02
items.description: [Hoverlab] A results directory rather than a reading list: search the situation, facet by entity count and ledger, and the aggregate claim sits at the bottom underneath the thirty-four rows it was computed from.

items.name: vijetbhat6/services-page-02
items.description: [Hoverlab] One productised engagement with the price in the first screen and no mandatory call — a fixed price behind a scoping call is consulting with extra steps. Includes the paragraph naming when it is the wrong shape.

items.name: vijetbhat6/integrations-index-page-02
items.description: [Hoverlab] Search-first, with facet counts including the zeroes — nobody browses an integration directory, and “Payroll (0)” answers the question inside the list the reader is already looking at.

items.name: vijetbhat6/integration-detail-page-02
items.description: [Hoverlab] The setup guide, not the pitch: what moves and which way, then a five-step wizard — written for the person turning the connector on rather than the one deciding to buy it.

items.name: vijetbhat6/alternatives-page-02
items.description: [Hoverlab] One rival, head to head, for a reader who already owns the competitor — so the argument is what a migration costs, and the page opens by telling roughly a third of its readers to stay where they are.

items.name: vijetbhat6/status-page-02
items.description: [Hoverlab] The status page read during diligence rather than during an outage: ninety days of uptime, the latency curve, and every incident carrying its post-mortem — including the bad one.

items.name: vijetbhat6/roadmap-page-02
items.description: [Hoverlab] Themes and refusals, no quarters — four problems stated as problems, plus the four things we have decided never to build, which is the section that takes nerve and the one customers actually need.

items.name: vijetbhat6/webinar-page-02
items.description: [Hoverlab] The replay, ungated, for the traffic that arrives months after the event — the gate moves to the transcript and the template, where it is a trade rather than a toll.

items.name: vijetbhat6/coming-soon-page-02
items.description: [Hoverlab] A referral queue with a real position: three places per invite, forty admitted a week, and the admission ceiling on the page rather than in the confirmation email — otherwise it is a dark pattern with a progress bar.

items.name: vijetbhat6/legal-page-02
items.description: [Hoverlab] One document with a plain-language column beside each clause, for the reader who cannot name the clause they need — and the cookie control inline, because a banner is unreachable the moment it has been dismissed.

items.name: vijetbhat6/community-page-02
items.description: [Hoverlab] The calendar is the community: the next session bookable in the first screen, the month underneath, and the chat links demoted to a strip — an idle Slack is a worse first impression than a half-full calendar.

items.name: vijetbhat6/affiliate-page-02
items.description: [Hoverlab] Proof before arithmetic — what four named partners actually earned last quarter, including the one for whom it is not working, and no calculator anywhere. A slider shows what you could earn from numbers you picked yourself.

items.name: vijetbhat6/testimonials-page-02
items.description: [Hoverlab] Segmented by who is talking rather than sorted by score, because a wall of forty quotes is uniformly impressive and uniformly irrelevant — with the full rating spread underneath, ones included.

items.name: vijetbhat6/gallery-page-02
items.description: [Hoverlab] The whole catalogue at once, filterable, with the total stated up front — the opposite trade to the switcher, and it honestly costs ninety images on load rather than one.

items.name: vijetbhat6/portfolio-index-page-02
items.description: [Hoverlab] One project per screen, four in total, each naming the constraint it worked around — nobody reads four case studies, and the constraint is the only sentence a competitor cannot copy.

items.name: vijetbhat6/btn-gradient
items.description: [Hoverlab] A button whose multi-color gradient slides across on hover, paired with a soft drop shadow that intensifies.

items.name: vijetbhat6/btn-neon
items.description: [Hoverlab] A bordered button with a soft cyan halo that fully ignites into a glowing pill on hover.

items.name: vijetbhat6/btn-3d
items.description: [Hoverlab] A chunky button with a solid drop-shadow base that compresses when pressed for a satisfying tactile feel.

items.name: vijetbhat6/btn-slide
items.description: [Hoverlab] A ghost button that fills from left to right with a solid color on hover, with the text color flipping in sync.

items.name: vijetbhat6/btn-border-draw
items.description: [Hoverlab] Minimal text button whose top and bottom borders sweep in from opposite directions on hover.

items.name: vijetbhat6/plasma-field
items.description: [Hoverlab] Four interfering sine waves coloured by their own interference. About fifteen instructions a pixel, which makes it the cheapest full-bleed background here.

items.name: vijetbhat6/liquid-metal
items.description: [Hoverlab] Noise sampled at a position that is itself noise, twice, then cut into contours so the folds read as a polished surface rather than as fog.

items.description: [Hoverlab] Thin-film interference: one phase read by three cosines a third of a turn apart, so the hue sweeps the whole palette instead of crossfading between two ends of it.

items.name: vijetbhat6/halftone-wave

items.name: vijetbhat6/metaball-lava
items.description: [Hoverlab] Six inverse-square fields thresholded into one body, so blobs grow a neck as they merge. No amount of border-radius produces a neck.

items.name: vijetbhat6/ferrofluid
items.description: [Hoverlab] A metaball field whose blobs grow spikes along the field lines, faded in toward the surface so the cores stay round. Almost entirely specular, like the real material.

items.name: vijetbhat6/lightning-arc
items.description: [Hoverlab] Three filaments on their own strike clocks, most cycles passing with nothing at all. A bolt that is always there is a squiggle; the waiting is the effect.

items.name: vijetbhat6/hyperspeed
items.description: [Hoverlab] Streaks accelerating out of a vanishing point, each hottest at its head. Done in polar coordinates, so 180 of them cost exactly what one does.

items.name: vijetbhat6/plasma-orb
items.description: [Hoverlab] A sphere with a turbulent surface, a fresnel rim and a halo that fades into the page rather than into a black square. Leans toward the pointer.

items.name: vijetbhat6/grid-distortion
items.description: [Hoverlab] A ruled grid where the space bends toward the pointer, not the lines. Two cells away the grid is exactly where it was.

items.description: [Hoverlab] A lattice of dots swelling with two waves — a slow one from the centre and a tight ring that arrives with the pointer. Each dot samples at its own cell, so it stays a grid.
